design_notes.field_naming: snake_case, globally unique across all sections and templates (machine-verified)
design_notes.section_prefixes: systemic review fields carry a system prefix (cvs_, resp_, gi_, neuro_, gu_, rheum_, heme_, endo_, derma_, psych_) so SQL queries like WHERE field_name LIKE 'cvs_%' are possible
design_notes.conditional_fields: A field carrying depends_on stays hidden until the parent field satisfies it. Supported operators: equals (match a stored value), not_equals, is_set (parent holds any non-null value).
design_notes.groups: An optional 'group' string renders a sub-header inside the section ListView (e.g. 'Menstrual History').
design_notes.red_flags: Fields with red_flag=true are danger symptoms: highlight them in the UI and surface them in the generated presentation. For dropdown/multi_select fields, red_flag applies to any non-None value.
design_notes.pertinent_negatives: Fields with pertinent_negative=true that end up false/None are joined into the 'denies ...' sentence of the case presentation.
design_notes.narrative_generation: For a true boolean, use 'narrative' if present, otherwise the lower-cased label. For dropdown/multi_select, use 'narrative' with {value} replaced by the stored value; when 'narrative' is absent fall back to '{label}: {value}'. Dropdown values equal to 'None', 'None reported', 'None identified' or null are treated as negative.
design_notes.value_encoding_for_sqlite: boolean -> INTEGER 0/1; number -> REAL; multi_select -> JSON array string in value_text; everything else -> TEXT

sections.title: Patient Demographics
sections.instruction: Open the encounter by introducing yourself, confirming patient identity, and documenting the informant and reliability.

fields.name: mrn
fields.label: Medical Record Number (MRN)
fields.hint: Hospital number if available

fields.name: occupation
fields.label: Occupation
fields.hint: e.g. farmer, teacher, driver, housewife - ask about exposures

fields.name: residence
fields.label: Residence
fields.hint: City / district / rural

sections.title: Chief Complaint (CC)
sections.instruction: List the main complaints in the patient's own words, each with its duration. Ask: 'What brought you to the hospital today?' Selecting a complaint automatically loads its detailed HPI template.

fields.name: cc_own_words
fields.label: Complaint in Patient's Own Words
fields.hint: e.g. 'I have a burning pain in my stomach'

sections.title: History of Present Illness (HPI) - General
sections.instruction: Expand each chief complaint: onset, course, context, treatment so far, and constitutional (B) symptoms. For pain complaints also complete the SOCRATES section and the matching complaint template.

fields.name: preceding_events
fields.label: Preceding / Triggering Events
fields.hint: e.g. trauma, new drug, stress, infection, exertion, food

fields.name: treatment_so_far
fields.label: Treatment Taken So Far
fields.hint: Self-medication, previous clinic or hospital visits for this illness

fields.name: constitutional_weight_loss_amount
fields.label: Amount of Weight Lost
fields.hint: e.g. 6 kg in 2 months

sections.title: Pain Assessment (SOCRATES)
sections.instruction: SOCRATES = Site, Onset, Character, Radiation, Associations, Timing, Exacerbating/Relieving factors, Severity. Complete for any significant pain complaint.

fields.name: socrates_site
fields.label: Site
fields.hint: Ask the patient to point with one finger

fields.name: socrates_radiation
fields.label: Radiation
fields.hint: e.g. to left arm, jaw, back, groin

sections.title: Cardiovascular System
sections.instruction: Screen for ischemia (chest pain), heart failure (exertional dyspnea, orthopnea, PND, edema), and arrhythmia (palpitations, syncope).

fields.name: cvs_dyspnea_exertion
fields.label: Exertional Dyspnea (NYHA)
options: On moderate exertion, 2 flights of stairs (NYHA II)
On minimal exertion, dressing or walking indoors (NYHA III)

sections.title: Respiratory System
sections.instruction: Cover cough, sputum, hemoptysis, breathlessness, wheeze and sleep-disordered breathing. Hemoptysis and stridor are red flags.

fields.name: resp_recurrent_infections
fields.label: Recurrent Chest Infections
fields.hint: More than 2 episodes per year

sections.title: Gastrointestinal System
sections.instruction: Cover the tract from mouth (dysphagia) to rectum (melena, tenesmus) plus hepatobiliary symptoms (jaundice, pale stools, dark urine).

fields.name: gi_dysphagia
fields.label: Dysphagia (Swallowing Difficulty)
options: To solids, now progressing to liquids
To both solids and liquids from the start

sections.title: Neurological System
sections.instruction: Screen higher functions, cranial nerves, motor, sensory, coordination and gait, plus sphincter function. Sudden-onset focal deficit is a red flag.

sections.title: Genitourinary System
sections.instruction: Screen urinary symptoms, renal colic, sexual health, and - for female patients - menstrual and obstetric history.

fields.name: gu_nocturia
fields.label: Nocturia
options: Three or more times per night

fields.name: gu_menstrual_flow
fields.label: Menstrual Flow
options: Heavy (soaking more than 1 pad per hour or clots)

sections.title: Rheumatology / Musculoskeletal System
sections.instruction: Define joint pain pattern (number, symmetry, small vs large, morning stiffness duration), plus extra-articular autoimmune features. A single hot swollen joint is septic arthritis until proven otherwise.

fields.name: rheum_hot_swollen_joint
fields.label: Single Hot Swollen Joint
fields.narrative: a single hot swollen joint (septic arthritis must be excluded)

fields.name: rheum_inflammatory_back_features
fields.label: Inflammatory Back Pain Features
options: Worse in the morning, improves with activity
Improves with exercise but not rest
Wakes the patient in the second half of the night

fields.name: rheum_proximal_weakness
fields.label: Proximal Muscle Weakness
fields.hint: Difficulty rising from a chair or combing hair

fields.name: rheum_genital_ulcers
fields.label: Genital Ulcers
fields.narrative: genital ulcers (with oral ulcers, consider Behcet disease)

fields.name: rheum_raynaud
fields.label: Raynaud Phenomenon
fields.hint: Color changes of fingers in cold

sections.title: Hematological / Lymphatic System
sections.instruction: Screen for anemia symptoms, bleeding tendency, lymphadenopathy and recurrent infection. Supraclavicular nodes and persistent unexplained lymphadenopathy are red flags.

sections.title: Endocrine System
sections.instruction: Screen thyrotoxicosis (heat intolerance, sweating, weight loss with good appetite), hypothyroidism (cold intolerance, weight gain), diabetes (polyuria, polydipsia, polyphagia) and adrenal/Cushing features.

sections.title: Skin (Integumentary) System
sections.instruction: A new rash with fever or after a new drug is a red flag (drug reaction, meningococcemia, vasculitis).

fields.name: derma_rash_detail
fields.label: Rash Details
fields.hint: Site, onset, spread, itch, fever, new drugs

sections.title: Psychiatric Screen
sections.instruction: Screen mood, sleep and anxiety. Any suicidal ideation is an emergency requiring immediate senior review.

sections.title: Past Medical History (PMH)
sections.instruction: Ask systematically: 'Do you have any of these conditions?' Tick and record duration and control for each positive answer.

fields.name: pmh_ckd_detail
fields.label: CKD Details
fields.hint: Stage / baseline creatinine

fields.name: pmh_malignancy_detail
fields.label: Cancer Details
fields.hint: Type, year, treatment received

fields.name: pmh_childhood_illnesses
fields.label: Childhood Illnesses
fields.hint: e.g. measles, chickenpox, rheumatic fever

sections.title: Past Surgical History (PSH)
sections.instruction: Tick previous operations and record the year plus any complications. Note anesthesia problems (relevant for future surgery).

fields.name: psh_operations_detail
fields.label: Operation Details
fields.hint: Operation, year, and any complications

fields.name: psh_anesthesia_problems
fields.label: Problems With Anesthesia
fields.hint: e.g. difficult intubation, post-op vomiting, malignant hyperthermia in family

sections.title: Drug History & Allergies
sections.instruction: Ask: 'What tablets, inhalers or injections do you take?' Include dose and frequency. Always ask separately about over-the-counter and herbal/traditional remedies.

fields.name: dh_anticoagulants
fields.label: Anticoagulants / Antiplatelets
fields.hint: warfarin, aspirin, clopidogrel, DOACs

sections.title: Family History (FH)
sections.instruction: Ask about parents, siblings and children: alive/dead, cause of death, chronic disease. Consanguinity and familial hemoglobinopathies are especially relevant in our region.

fields.name: fh_father_detail
fields.label: Father's Illness / Cause of Death
fields.hint: Condition + age at death if applicable

fields.name: fh_conditions_specify
fields.label: Specify Relative + Condition
fields.hint: e.g. father - MI at 50

fields.name: fh_sudden_death
fields.label: Sudden Unexplained Death Before 40 in Family

sections.title: Social History (SH)
sections.instruction: Smoking (calculate pack-years), alcohol, substances, occupation exposures, living conditions, diet and stressors - these often explain the diagnosis.

fields.name: sh_pack_years
fields.label: Pack-Years
fields.hint: (cigarettes per day / 20) x years - can be auto-calculated

fields.name: sh_stressors
fields.label: Recent Stressors
fields.hint: e.g. bereavement, finances, conflict, exams

sections.title: Student Clinical Reasoning
sections.instruction: Now synthesize: summarize the case, commit to a differential list, and plan initial investigations. This section is the teaching core of the module.

fields.name: cr_summary
fields.label: Student Summary
fields.hint: Summarize in 3-5 sentences: who, presenting problem, key positives and negatives

fields.name: cr_investigations
fields.label: Planned Initial Investigations
fields.hint: e.g. CBC, renal and liver panels, ECG, chest X-ray, urinalysis

hpi_complaint_templates.title: Chest Pain - Detailed HPI
hpi_complaint_templates.instruction: Differentiate cardiac (crushing, exertional, radiating, GTN-responsive), dissection (tearing to back), pericarditic (positional), pleuritic and GI causes. The associated red flags demand urgent ECG.

fields.name: cp_pattern
fields.label: Pattern
options: On exertion only, relieved by rest (stable angina)

fields.name: cp_chest_wall_tenderness
fields.label: Pain Reproducible by Pressing the Chest Wall

fields.name: cp_red_flags
fields.label: Red Flags Present
options: Tearing pain radiating to the back (dissection)
Pain lasting more than 20 minutes unrelieved by rest or GTN

hpi_complaint_templates.title: Shortness of Breath - Detailed HPI
hpi_complaint_templates.instruction: Grade severity with the MRC dyspnea scale, define tempo of onset (sudden = PE/pneumothorax, days = pneumonia, months = HF/COPD), and screen for orthopnea and PND.

fields.name: dysp_mrc_grade
fields.label: MRC Dyspnea Grade
options: 2 - Hurries on level ground / slight hill
3 - Walks slower than peers, stops on level ground
4 - Stops after about 100 m or a few minutes

fields.name: dysp_progression
fields.label: Progression
options: Episodic with full recovery between attacks

hpi_complaint_templates.title: Cough - Detailed HPI
hpi_complaint_templates.instruction: Classify duration (acute <3 weeks, subacute 3-8 weeks, chronic >8 weeks) and productivity. Weight loss + night sweats + hemoptysis in a smoker or TB contact = investigate urgently.

fields.name: cx_hemoptysis_amount
fields.label: Hemoptysis Amount
fields.hint: Streaks vs frank blood vs clots

fields.name: cx_red_flags
fields.label: Red Flags Present
options: Smoker over 45 with new or changed cough

hpi_complaint_templates.title: Fever - Detailed HPI
hpi_complaint_templates.instruction: Define the fever pattern, height and duration, then hunt the source: travel, raw milk (brucellosis), sick contacts, TB exposure, animal exposure. This template pairs with the full systemic review.

hpi_complaint_templates.title: Abdominal Pain - Detailed HPI
hpi_complaint_templates.instruction: Apply SOCRATES tailored to the abdomen: site, migration (periumbilical to RIF = appendicitis; flank to groin = ureteric colic), character (colicky vs constant), food relation, and obstruction screen. Pain before vomiting suggests a surgical cause.

hpi_complaint_templates.title: Jaundice - Detailed HPI
hpi_complaint_templates.instruction: Classify pre-hepatic / hepatic / post-hepatic from the history: pale stools + dark urine + pruritus = obstructive. Hunt viral risk factors and always screen for encephalopathy and bleeding (acute liver failure).

hpi_complaint_templates.title: Headache - Detailed HPI
hpi_complaint_templates.instruction: Separate primary (migraine / tension / cluster) from secondary headache using red flags: thunderclap onset, fever with neck stiffness, new neurology, morning worsening with vomiting, new headache over 50.

fields.name: ha_frequency
fields.label: Frequency
options: Nocturnal attacks at the same time daily (cluster)

fields.name: ha_analgesic_overuse
fields.label: Analgesic Use More Than 10 Days per Month

fields.name: ha_red_flags
fields.label: Red Flags Present
options: Worse in the morning with vomiting (raised ICP)
Painful red eye with halos (acute glaucoma)

hpi_complaint_templates.title: Palpitations - Detailed HPI
hpi_complaint_templates.instruction: Ask the patient to tap out the rhythm. Sudden-onset sudden-offset regular tachycardia suggests SVT; irregular suggests atrial fibrillation. Red flags: syncope, chest pain, family history of sudden death.

fields.name: pal_estimated_rate
fields.label: Patient-Estimated Heart Rate (bpm)
fields.hint: Ask the patient to tap the rhythm on their chest

hpi_complaint_templates.title: Dizziness / Syncope - Detailed HPI
hpi_complaint_templates.instruction: First classify: lightheadedness (presyncope), vertigo (spin), or disequilibrium. Then separate vasovagal from cardiac syncope (exertional, no prodrome, injury = cardiac). Tongue biting + postictal confusion = seizure.

fields.name: diz_postictal_confusion
fields.label: Prolonged Confusion After the Episode
fields.narrative: postictal-like confusion after the episode (suggests seizure)

fields.name: diz_tongue_biting
fields.label: Tongue Biting or Incontinence During Episode

hpi_complaint_templates.title: Urinary Symptoms - Detailed HPI
hpi_complaint_templates.instruction: Separate lower UTI (cystitis: dysuria, frequency, suprapubic pain) from upper UTI (pyelonephritis: fever, rigors, loin pain). In elderly men think of retention and prostatism; confusion in the elderly may be the only UTI sign.

lab_references.note: Eosinophilia: allergy, asthma, parasites, drug reactions

lab_references.critical_low: below 50,000 bleeding risk; below 20,000 spontaneous bleeding

lab_references.note: Classify anemia: microcytic below 80, normocytic 80-100, macrocytic above 100
Low in marrow failure; high in hemolysis or after iron therapy
Hemolysed sample falsely raises K+
Correct for albumin: add 0.8 x (4.0 - albumin in g/dL)
Also raised in bone disease and pregnancy
Clinically visible jaundice usually above 2.5 - 3 mg/dL
Monitors warfarin; prolonged INR in cholestasis and liver failure
Monitors unfractionated heparin
High-sensitivity assays use the 99th percentile cutoff; interpret rise AND fall
BNP below 100 makes heart failure unlikely
100-125 prediabetes; 126 or more (on two occasions) = diabetes
200 or more with symptoms = diabetes
5.7-6.4% prediabetes; 6.5% or more = diabetes
Above 4 with acidosis suggests tissue hypoperfusion / sepsis
High in iron deficiency; low in chronic disease
20-29 insufficient; below 20 deficient
Only rules out VTE when pretest probability is low; use age x 0.01 cutoff above age 50
More specific than amylase for pancreatitis
Appears when plasma glucose exceeds ~180 mg/dL (renal threshold)

clinical_pearls.pearl: Classify anemia by MCV: microcytic (<80) = iron deficiency, thalassemia, chronic disease; normocytic (80-100) = acute blood loss, CKD, marrow failure; macrocytic (>100) = B12/folate deficiency, alcohol, hypothyroidism, reticulocytosis.
Mentzer index (MCV / RBC count in millions): below 13 suggests thalassemia trait; above 13 suggests iron deficiency. RDW is high in iron deficiency but usually normal in thalassemia trait.
BUN/creatinine ratio above 20 (using mg/dL) suggests a pre-renal cause (dehydration, heart failure) or GI bleeding (protein load).
A 'normal' creatinine does not guarantee normal renal function in elderly or low-muscle-mass patients - always calculate eGFR.

Hepatocellular pattern: AST/ALT markedly raised with mild ALP rise. Cholestatic pattern: ALP and GGT markedly raised with mild transaminase rise. AST:ALT ratio above 2 with raised GGT suggests alcohol-related liver disease.
An isolated ALP rise should be confirmed with GGT: high GGT = hepatic origin; normal GGT = bone origin (or pregnancy).

Dark urine + pale stools indicates conjugated hyperbilirubinemia (obstructive). Unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia (hemolysis, Gilbert) does not darken the urine because unconjugated bilirubin is albumin-bound and not filtered.
Corrected calcium = measured calcium + 0.8 x (4.0 - serum albumin in g/dL). Interpret total calcium only after correction.
In hyponatremia always check serum osmolality first (estimated: 2xNa + glucose/18 + BUN/2.8) to exclude pseudohyponatremia, then assess volume status and urine sodium.
Potassium below 2.5 or above 6.5 mEq/L is life-threatening - obtain an immediate ECG. Exclude pseudohyperkalemia (hemolysed sample) before treating.
Anion gap = Na - (Cl + HCO3), normal 8-12 mEq/L. High gap acidosis mnemonic MUDPILES: Methanol, Uremia, DKA, Propylene glycol, Isoniazid/Iron, Lactate, Ethylene glycol, Salicylates.
D-dimer is only useful to RULE OUT PE/DVT when the pretest probability is low (e.g. Wells score low). A positive D-dimer is not diagnostic - it mandates imaging.
Troponin must show a rise and/or fall with at least one value above the 99th percentile to diagnose myocardial infarction; a single static mild rise occurs in CKD, heart failure and sepsis.
CRP rises within hours and falls quickly on recovery; ESR changes slowly and is affected by age, anemia and pregnancy. Both are non-specific screening markers.
Ferritin is an acute-phase reactant: a normal or high ferritin does NOT exclude iron deficiency in inflammation or chronic disease - check transferrin saturation or soluble transferrin receptor.
INR monitors warfarin (extrinsic pathway); aPTT monitors unfractionated heparin (intrinsic pathway). Isolated prolonged aPTT with bleeding think hemophilia; with clotting think lupus anticoagulant.
Hyperglycemia with ketonuria, vomiting and Kussmaul breathing = DKA until proven otherwise: send glucose, ABG (pH, bicarbonate) and ketones.

case_presentation.description: Rules for auto-assembling a formal Internal Medicine case presentation paragraph from the stored field values of a completed encounter.

rules.pronom: Use he/his for Male, she/her for Female (key: pronoun).
rules.title: Mr. for Male, Ms. for Female.
rules.booleans: A true boolean contributes its 'narrative' phrase, or the lower-cased label when 'narrative' is absent. False booleans are silent unless pertinent_negative=true (then they feed the 'denies' sentence).
rules.dropdowns_and_multi_select: Values equal to 'None', 'None reported', 'None identified', 'Not applicable' or null are treated as negative and skipped. Otherwise use 'narrative' with {value} replaced, or fall back to '{label}: {value}'.
rules.list_joining: Join phrases with ', ' and place ' and ' before the final phrase.
rules.pmh_pairing: When a pmh boolean is true and its paired _years field is set, render '<label> for <years> years'. Add the control field when set (e.g. 'poorly controlled').
rules.priority: If a symptom appears both in an HPI complaint template and the systemic review, the template value takes precedence in the narrative.
rules.negatives_scope: State pertinent negatives mainly from the system matching the chief complaint - a good presentation does not read the entire review of systems aloud.
rules.occupation_phrase: 'a/an ' + occupation, omitted entirely when occupation is empty.

templates.opening: {title} {patient_name}, a {age_years}-year-old {gender}{occupation_phrase}, {marital_status}, presented to the {encounter_setting} with a {cc_1_duration_value}-{cc_1_duration_unit} history of {cc_1}.
templates.socrates_detail: The pain is {socrates_character_lower} in character, located {socrates_site}, radiating to {socrates_radiation}, with severity {socrates_severity}/10. It is worse with {socrates_exacerbating} and relieved by {socrates_relieving}.
templates.red_flag_close: Red flags identified in this history: {red_flag_list}.
templates.smoking_sentence: a current smoker with {sh_pack_years} pack-years / an ex-smoker with {sh_pack_years} pack-years / a never-smoker.

case_presentation.example_output: Mr. Ahmed Ali, a 58-year-old male, a farmer by occupation, Married, presented to the Emergency department with a 2-Days history of Chest pain. The Chest pain began Sudden (seconds to minutes) and has been Progressively worsening. The pain is Crushing / pressure / squeezing in character, located Central / retrosternal, radiating to Left arm, with severity 8/10. It is worse with Exertion and relieved by Rest (within minutes). It is associated with sweating (diaphoresis) and nausea. Systemic review reveals exertional dyspnea (On minimal exertion, dressing or walking indoors (NYHA III)), orthopnea (2 pillows) and pitting edema up to Ankles only. He denies palpitations, hemoptysis, melena, jaundice or dysphagia. Past medical history includes Hypertension for 10 years (poorly controlled) and Diabetes Mellitus (Type 2) for 8 years on oral agents. Current medications: metformin 500 mg TDS, amlodipine 5 mg OD. Allergies: none known. Family history: father died of MI at age 50. He is a current smoker with a 30 pack-year history. Red flags identified in this history: Pain lasting more than 20 minutes unrelieved by rest or GTN.

sqlite_schema.strategy: Entity-Attribute-Value (EAV) for flexible, schema-driven form data + normalized tables for repeatable rows (medications, differentials). This JSON schema lives in app assets and drives dynamic form rendering, so no table migration is needed when the question set evolves.

columns: patient_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES patients(patient_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
encounter_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES encounters(encounter_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
tables.notes: Store booleans as 0/1, numbers in value_number, everything else (including multi_select as a JSON array string) in value_text. Auto-save each change with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(encounter_id, field_name) DO UPDATE.

columns: encounter_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES encounters(encounter_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
encounter_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES encounters(encounter_id) ON DELETE CASCADE

indexes: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_responses_encounter ON responses(encounter_id)
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_encounters_patient ON encounters(patient_id)
flutter_implementation_notes: Ship this JSON as an asset (declare in pubspec.yaml under assets/) and parse it once at startup: rootBundle.loadString + jsonDecode.
In sqflite onConfigure run: PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON.
Render each section as a ListView of field widgets dispatched by field type (checkbox for boolean, DropdownButton for dropdown, chips for multi_select, text fields otherwise).
Honor depends_on reactively: hide a field until its parent satisfies equals / not_equals / is_set, and clear dependent values when the parent changes.
Use the section prefixes (cvs_, resp_, gi_, ...) for scoped queries such as WHERE field_name LIKE 'cvs_%'.
list_repeater fields (medications, differentials) persist to their dedicated tables, not to responses.
Generate the case presentation by walking case_presentation.generation_order and joining the stored values per case_presentation.rules.
Cache lab_references in a local table on first launch to allow offline search and user favorites later.
